about: Every sentence, label and English word list the mind map uses. Placeholders are {name}. A project overrides any key in .devops/mindmap/text.json with the same shape ({"text": {...}, "words": {...}}); keys it leaves out keep these defaults.

text.overviewSize: **Size:** {codeFiles} code files ({languages}), {docs} docs, {modules} modules, {symbols} functions and types.
text.warnDuplicates: {count} name(s) defined in more than one file ({names})
text.warnUndeclared: {count} imported package(s) not in a manifest (standard library or missing)
text.overviewFooter: _Mind map of {date}. Details: `.devops/mindmap/MINDMAP.md`; exact lookups: `mindmap_query` (symbol, file, module, library, search)._
text.summaryGenerated: Generated {date} by `mindmap_build` (`devops-mindmap build --save`). Do not edit by hand.
text.summaryCounts: {codeFiles} code files, {docs} docs, {modules} modules, {symbols} symbols, {calls} call links, {libraries} libraries.
text.summaryHowTo: **How to use it.** Read the overview below for a question about the project; read on for the detail. Ask `mindmap_query` (symbol, file, module, library, search) for exact definitions, signatures, callers, importers, tests and docs instead of reading files to find them. Run `mindmap_status` first: only the files it lists as changed need re-reading. Before writing a new function, look it up here and in **Possible duplicates**.
text.treeIntro: The mind map is a tree (project > module > file > class > function, and doc > section) with cross links (imports, calls, documents, tests, uses). `mindmap_tree` opens any node with its documentation, notes and links.
text.codeTreeIntro: Each line: name or signature, kind, lines, then what its doc comment, docstring, README or note says. Private helpers without documentation are left out; `mindmap_tree` on a file lists all of them.
text.docsToCodeIntro: Which doc sections describe which functions and files.
text.modulesColumns: | Module | Files | Languages | Depends on | Used by | Libraries | Key exports |
text.modulesOmitted: {count} smaller modules omitted; query them by name.
text.docsOmitted: {count} more docs; query a file to see which docs cover it.
text.librariesColumns: | Library | Declared in | Used by files | Note |
text.libraryUndeclared: not in a manifest (standard library, or missing)
text.duplicatesIntro: The same name is defined in more than one file. Check before adding another; extend one instead.
text.limitsNote: Heuristic (regular expressions, no compiler): dynamic imports, reflection, macros, overloads and same-named methods on different types are not told apart. A call is linked only when the callee is in the same file, a file it imports, or defined once in the project. Read the file before relying on a link for a change.
text.notesHeader:
# Mind map notes

Hand-written notes that the mind map attaches to its nodes; rebuilding the map never touches this file. One section per node, headed `## <node>`: a module (`src/api`), a file (`src/api/routes.ts`), a function or type (`src/api/routes.ts#routeFor`, or the bare name when it is defined once), a doc (`docs/guide.md`) or `project`. Say how it works, why it is built that way, and what to watch out for.
text.sourceSavedQuery: saved map from {date} (run mindmap_status to see what changed since)
text.sourceBuiltKeep: built now, not saved (mindmap_build with save=true keeps it)
text.statusNoMap: No saved mind map: run mindmap_build with save=true.
text.statusStale: Re-read only the files listed, then run mindmap_build with save=true so the next seat starts from a current map.
text.statusCurrent: The saved map is current: trust it and do not re-read files to rediscover structure.
text.overviewChanged: {count} file(s) changed since: {files}. Read those directly if the question touches them; rebuild with mindmap_build save=true.
text.warnDefinedTwice: defined in more than one place: check for duplicate implementations
text.libraryNotFound: Not declared in a manifest and not imported by scanned code.
text.errNodeString: node must be a string of 1 to 300 characters
text.errNoteHeading: text may not contain a "## " heading line
text.errQueryOne: ask exactly one of: symbol, file, module, library, search
text.errQueryString: the query must be a string of 1 to 300 characters
text.errNotInMap: not in the mind map: {file} (not a code or doc file, skipped, or the map is stale)
text.cliUsage: usage: devops-mindmap overview [--json] | tree [--node ID] [--depth N] [--json] | note --node ID --text TEXT [--apply] | build [--save] [--json] | status | query --symbol NAME|--file PATH|--module ID|--library NAME|--search TEXT [--fresh]   [--dest DIR]
text.chatPrompt: Project mind map (quick scan, generated; no command needed, with or without the DevOps team). When the person asks about this project in plain words, answer from it first; for how something works use the mindmap_tree MCP tool, for other specifics mindmap_query, and open files only at the line ranges they give. It can be out of date: mindmap_status says which files changed; read those directly, and when the person asks to refresh the map, call mindmap_build with save=true.
text.chatNoMap: No mind map saved yet: when the person asks about the project or asks for a map, mindmap_build with save=true builds one.
text.serverInstructions: Repository mind map, with or without the DevOps team: for any question about the project in plain chat (what it is, how it is laid out, where something is, what uses what), call mindmap_overview first and answer from it, then mindmap_tree for how a function or module works (its documentation, note and neighbours) or mindmap_query for specifics, and open files only at the line ranges it gives. In a DevOps team run the Researcher owns the map: mindmap_status, then mindmap_build with save=true when stale, and the brief carries what other seats need.
text.toolOverview: Quick scan of the project for plain chat, with or without the DevOps team: what it is (from the README), size and languages, where it starts, how it is run (scripts, make targets), its parts and what each is for, which docs to read first, the most depended-on files, main libraries and what to watch out for, in about forty lines. Uses the saved map (and says how many files changed since) or builds one in memory. Call it first for any question about the project. Read-only.
text.toolTree: Open one node of the mind map tree (project > module > file > class > function; documentation > folder > doc > section; libraries) with its documentation: the doc comment or docstring, the README or file header that describes it, the hand-written note for it, its subtree to `depth`, and its links both ways grouped by kind (imports, calls, uses, documents, links, tests) with each neighbour's own documentation. Use it to explain how a function or module works without opening files. `node` is a path, `path#name`, a module, a bare name defined once, a doc path or `project`. Read-only.
text.toolNote: Write how a module, file, function, type or doc works into the mind map: adds or replaces that node's section in .devops/mindmap/NOTES.md, hand-written documentation that rebuilding never overwrites and that mindmap_tree, mindmap_query and the overview show with the node. Plans unless apply=true.
text.toolBuild: The repository mind map, so seats stop re-reading files to rediscover structure: documentation (title, summary, headings, links), modules (files, languages, dependencies both ways, libraries, key exports), every code file (hash, imports, importers, libraries, tests, docs) and its functions, classes and types (signature and line range), call links between functions, libraries (declared in which manifest, used by which files, undeclared or unused) and names defined in more than one file (possible duplicate implementations). Returns a compact Markdown summary; with save=true writes .devops/mindmap/OVERVIEW.md (the quick scan), MINDMAP.md (the tree with documentation, then the detail), graph.json (the tree and its cross links) and mindmap.json (for queries). Doc comments, docstrings, file headers, READMEs, doc sections that name a function or file, and the hand-written NOTES.md are all attached to the nodes they describe. Sentences and word lists come from mindmap-text.json, overridable per project in .devops/mindmap/text.json. Heuristic (no compiler). Runs no program.
text.toolStatus: Compare the saved mind map with the files on disk: which code and doc files changed, were added or were removed, and which modules they belong to. Re-read only those files; trust the map for the rest. Read-only.
text.toolQuery: Ask the mind map one question instead of reading files: `symbol` (where it is defined, its signature and line range, callers, callees, tests, docs; a warning when defined twice), `file` (symbols with line ranges, imports, importers, libraries, tests, docs, calls in and out), `module` (files, dependencies both ways, libraries, exports), `library` (manifest, version, files using it) or `search` (names, paths and doc titles containing the text). Uses the saved map unless fresh=true. Read-only.
text.errTextShape: must be an object with "text" and/or "words"
text.errTextValue: {section}.{key} has the wrong type or size
text.paramFull: Also return the whole map as data (large; prefer mindmap_query).
